chains.title: GABPA binds the C250T alt allele and activates TERT
chains.element: TERT promoter C250T de novo ETS motif

links.claim: The alt A allele is predicted to create a de novo ETS motif that GABPA binds more strongly than the ref G allele; QBiC-SELEX coverage was not checked and no QBiC evidence was supplied.
C250T lies in the TERT promoter and is proposed to act as an allele-specific GABPA-responsive promoter element.
Increased GABPA occupancy at the alt allele is proposed to increase TERT transcription.
The effect is proposed in glioblastoma cells, matching the DepMap glioblastoma expression context; melanoma and bladder cancer may share the mechanism.
Increased TERT expression and telomerase activity would support immortalization and tumor growth.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR or ChIP-seq shows enrichment on the alt allele over ref at the TERT promoter.
GABPA knockdown or CRISPRi reduces TERT expression preferentially in C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma cells.
Ref versus alt TERT promoter reporters differ in activity in a GABPA-dependent manner.
falsified_if: The alt allele is not preferentially bound by GABPA in an appropriate heterozygous cell system.
GABPA loss does not reduce TERT expression or reporter activity from the alt promoter.
Allele-specific TERT expression is explained by a linked variant rather than C250T.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect; C250T is passenger or linked to the causal variant
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at C250T is detectable.
Ref and alt TERT promoter reporters show no reproducible allelic difference.
Any TERT association is explained by a linked causal variant or by passenger mutation at a mutational hotspot.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA binding and GABPA-dependent TERT activation are demonstrated for C250T.

chains.title: ETS1 binds the C250T alt allele and activates TERT
chains.element: TERT promoter C250T de novo ETS motif

links.claim: The alt A allele is predicted to create an ETS motif bound more strongly by ETS1 than the ref G allele; QBiC-SELEX coverage was not checked.
C250T is proposed to form an allele-specific ETS1-responsive element in the TERT promoter.
Increased ETS1 occupancy at the alt allele is proposed to increase TERT transcription.
This chain is proposed in glioblastoma cells, with possible relevance to melanoma and bladder cancer.
Increased TERT/telomerase would promote replicative immortality.

predictions: Allele-specific ETS1 ChIP shows preferential binding to the alt allele.
ETS1 knockdown reduces TERT expression or alt-promoter reporter activity.
falsified_if: ETS1 does not bind the C250T alt allele preferentially.
ETS1 loss does not affect TERT expression from the alt promoter.

matrix.test: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR or ChIP-seq at the TERT promoter in heterozygous C250T glioblastoma cells

outcomes.outcome: alt allele is enriched over ref for GABPA
ETS1, not GABPA, shows preferential alt-allele binding
ETS2, not GABPA, shows preferential alt-allele binding

matrix.test: GABPA knockdown or CRISPRi followed by TERT qPCR in C250T-heterozygous versus TERT-wild-type glioblastoma cells

outcomes.outcome: TERT decreases preferentially in C250T-heterozygous cells

matrix.test: Ref versus alt TERT promoter luciferase reporter in a glioblastoma line, with and without GABPA knockdown

outcomes.outcome: alt reporter is higher and the difference is GABPA-dependent
alt reporter is higher but GABPA-independent
alt reporter is higher but GABPA-independent

next_experiment: Run a ref-versus-alt TERT promoter luciferase reporter assay in a glioblastoma line, with and without GABPA knockdown; this is the cheapest test that separates GABPA-dependent activation (H1) from no allelic effect (H4).
